subject.title: Bug: Billing error (402) causes infinite retry death spiral for inline-apiKey providers (no backoff)

question: Should OpenClaw make inline `models.providers.<id>.apiKey` credentials participate in persisted provider-level auth/billing cooldowns, even though that fail-closes existing inline-key configs during cooldown windows?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the durable cooldown identity, persistence, and fail-closed upgrade behavior are auth-provider policy choices before the linked PR should land.

options.title: Accept provider-level inline cooldown
options.body: Land or rebuild the linked fix so literal, env, and SecretRef inline API keys get billing/auth cooldown protection without requiring auth profiles.

options.title: Keep cooldowns profile-only
options.body: Document auth-profile migration as the supported workaround and close the linked implementation path as not planned.

options.title: Request narrower auth design
options.body: Pause the linked PR until maintainers specify the exact inline cooldown namespace, recovery behavior, and public helper surface they want.

recommendation.title: Accept provider-level inline cooldown
recommendation.body: Land or rebuild the linked fix so literal, env, and SecretRef inline API keys get billing/auth cooldown protection without requiring auth profiles.

likelyOwner.reason: Among the observed routing candidates, `steipete` is tied to recent adjacent model-auth work and repeated issue timeline routing for this auth/provider policy choice.
